card.title: 92. INFANTRY REGIMENT
card.text: Deployment: Develop BLITZKRIEG, SKY BARONS or TACTICAL STRIKE.
card.flavorText: During WWII; the 92nd Infantry Regiment served within the German 2nd Infantry Division, which was restructured into the 2nd Motorized Infantry Division in 1940. Originally formed in 1934 and based in Cottbus, the division drew its manpower largely from central Germany. It first saw combat during the invasion of Poland in 1939, where it participated in rapid advances as part of Army Group South. The unit then shifted westward for the 1940 campaign in France, moving through Belgium and into northern France with Army Group A. Following the French armistice, the division was reorganized into a motorized formation, enhancing its speed and operational flexibility. As the 2nd Motorized Infantry Division, it took part in Operation Barbarossa in June 1941 under Army Group Centre. It advanced deep into Soviet territory, fighting at key locations like Smolensk and later near Moscow. The division suffered severe losses during the Soviet winter counteroffensive. The relentless fighting on the Eastern Front wore down its strength, leading to its withdrawal and conversion into the 12th Panzer Division in 1942. This marked a further shift toward mechanization as the Wehrmacht adapted to the demands of mobile warfare on the vast Soviet front.
